source.title: Primary School Education Curriculum Design — Christian Religious Education, Grade 6
source.notes: Read in full via the Read tool (no pages param). First published 2021, Revised 2024. 5 strands: 1.0 Creation, 2.0 The Bible, 3.0 The Life of Jesus Christ, 4.0 The Church, 5.0 Christian Living Today (22 sub-strands total). Lesson-count discrepancies exist across three locations in the source PDF (the front-matter Summary of Strands and Sub Strands table, each sub-strand's own body header, and the Appendix 1 assessment-methods table) — e.g. 1.1 My Purpose is listed as 5 lessons in the summary table but 4 in both the body header and the appendix; 3.1 Call of Disciples is listed as 4 in the body header but 5 in both the summary table and appendix. lessonCount below uses the majority value across the three locations (2-of-3), consistent with the precedent already established for other grades' front-matter-vs-body discrepancies. A second discrepancy, structurally identical to the one already documented in the Grade 7 CRE record: sub-strand 3.4 is titled 'Faith in God' in the front-matter summary table and in Appendix 1, but the actual body text (which carries the outcomes/experiences/KIQ) titles it '3.4 Miracle of Healing' and its content is specifically the healing of the bleeding woman (Luke 8:43-48), with the Key Inquiry Question 'How did the bleeding woman portray faith in God?'. Body text is treated as authoritative; the table's 'Faith in God' label is retained parenthetically since it names the sub-strand's thematic thread. Appendix 1 also lists sub-strands 5.3 and 5.4 in swapped order relative to the body/summary-table order (Alcohol/Drugs before Sanctity of Life) — treated as an appendix ordering quirk, not a content discrepancy; body/table order (Sanctity of Life then Alcohol/Drugs/Substance Abuse) is used here.

subStrands.name: 1.1 My Purpose (Talents and Abilities)
specificLearningOutcomes: discuss how they use their God-given talents and abilities
explain biblical teachings on the use of talents and abilities
identify values required to nurture talents and abilities
utilise God-given talents and abilities to serve others
keyInquiryQuestions: How do you use your God-given talents and abilities?
learningExperiences: list the different talents and abilities they possess
discuss how they use their God-given talents and abilities
participate in different activities to nurture their talents and abilities
in turns, read Exodus 31:3 and share what they have learnt
read Romans 12:4 and discuss lessons learnt
list values that can help them develop and sustain their God-given talents and abilities
use their God-given talents and abilities to serve others
compose a poem on 'how I use my talents and abilities'
linkedLearningAreas: English: communication skills are enhanced as learners read and participate in class discussions.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose a poem on 'how I use my talents and abilities'.

subStrands.name: 1.2 Marriage and Family
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the biblical teachings on marriage and family
discuss the negative results of early marriage
identify values needed to avoid early marriage
desire to uphold Christian values to avoid early marriage
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is marriage an important institution?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the word, 'marriage'
share experiences of how they relate with other members of their families
use a digital device or a chart to write messages on how families should relate with each other
in groups, role-play how a Christian family should relate with each other
in pairs, read Genesis 2:21-24 and discuss what the Bible teaches about marriage
discuss, collaboratively, why early marriages should be discouraged in society today
list values that young people should uphold to avoid early marriage
develop posters with messages discouraging early marriage
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read, discuss and write messages discouraging early marriage today.
Science and Technology: learners use digital devices to write messages on how families should relate with each other.

subStrands.name: 1.3 Leisure
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the biblical teaching on God's rest
explain biblical teachings on good use of leisure
describe how youths misuse leisure time today
identify values needed for appropriate use of leisure time
desire to use leisure time responsibly
keyInquiryQuestions: How can youths avoid misuse of leisure time?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the meaning of the word, 'leisure'
share with a classmate how they use their leisure time
list different activities they do during their leisure time
read Genesis 2:1-3 and state why God rested
read 1 Timothy 5:13 and state the importance of leisure time
list ways in which youths misuse leisure time today
list values which can help youths to use leisure time well
write a reflection journal on positive ways of spending leisure time
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read the Bible and outline the importance of leisure time.

subStrands.name: 2.1 The Inspired Word of God
specificLearningOutcomes: explain why the Bible is the inspired word of God
name three authors who wrote the Bible
discuss reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages
outline the advantages of translating the Bible into local languages
read the Bible always to get spiritual nourishment
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the Bible different from other books?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the meaning of 'Bible is the inspired Word of God'
compose and sing a song on 'the Bible as an inspired Word of God'
read 2 Timothy 3:16-17 and explain the meaning of the text
name authors who were inspired to write the Old and New Testament
use digital devices to search for reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages
identify the advantages of translating the Bible into local languages
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing a song on, 'The Bible as an inspired Word of God.'
Science and Technology skills are applied as learners use digital devices to search for reasons that led to translation of the Bible into local languages.

subStrands.name: 2.2 The Ten Commandments
specificLearningOutcomes: outline the Ten Commandments and their importance
identify values and life skills in the Ten Commandments
outline lessons learnt from the Ten Commandments
appreciate the importance of obeying the Ten Commandments
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you obey the Ten Commandments?
learningExperiences: team up to brainstorm on the meaning of the word, 'Commandment'
read Exodus 20:3-17 and list the Ten Commandments
discuss how the Ten Commandments help Christians live well with God and others
discuss with peers the values and life skills found in the Ten Commandments
discuss lessons learnt from the Ten Commandments
design a poster or a chart and write the Ten Commandments, display the chart at the CRE learning corner
watch a video clip of Moses and the Ten Commandments
linkedLearningAreas: English: communication skills are enhanced as learners compose and recite poems about the Ten Commandments.
Social Studies skills are enhanced through the concept of human rights and good neighbourliness.

subStrands.name: 2.3 Bible Stories — Samson Defeats the Philistines
specificLearningOutcomes: retell the story of Samson as guided by the scriptures
outline ways Christians depend on God to overcome challenges in life
list lessons learnt from the story of Samson
depend on God in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should you depend on God?
learningExperiences: team up to read Judges 15:14-17 and retell the story
retell how God gave Samson power to defeat his enemies
list ways Christians depend on God's power to overcome daily challenges
work with peers to list lessons learnt from the story of Samson
compose a poem on the importance of depending on God
linkedLearningAreas: English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read and retell the story of Samson.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose a poem on the importance of depending on God's power.

subStrands.name: 2.4 Faith in God — Elisha
specificLearningOutcomes: describe how Elisha recovered the axe head
exercise faith in God to overcome challenges in life
trust in God's power when faced with challenges
keyInquiryQuestions: How did Elisha recover the axe head?
learningExperiences: in pairs, brainstorm on challenges they experience in life and how they deal with them
read 2 Kings 6:1-7 and retell the story
use a digital device to watch a video clip about the story
discuss ways they exercise faith in God to overcome challenges in life
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology skills are applied as learners use digital devices to perform tasks.

subStrands.name: 2.5 Jacob Wrestles an Angel
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate the story of Jacob as guided by the scriptures
outline lessons learnt from the story of Jacob
identify values learnt from the story of Jacob
emulate Jacob by being persistent in prayer
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it good to pray always?
learningExperiences: in turns, read Genesis 32:22-30 and retell the story
watch a video clip of Jacob wrestling with God
role-play the story of Jacob wrestling with God
brainstorm on the meaning of 'persistence in prayer'
discuss lessons learnt from the story
discuss how they apply lessons learnt in their lives
compose and say a prayer to God
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts: creative skills are exhibited as learners compose and sing a song on persistence in prayers.
Science and Technology skills are applied as learners watch a video clip on Jacob wrestling with God.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners take turns to read the Bible.

subStrands.name: 3.1 The Call of the Disciples
specificLearningOutcomes: retell the call of the first disciples as guided by the scriptures
state how different people are called to serve God today
serve God in his or her daily life to grow spiritually
keyInquiryQuestions: How did the disciples respond to the call of Jesus Christ?
learningExperiences: discuss, in small groups, different roles they play in church and share in class
in turns, read Mark 1:16-20 and retell the call of the first disciples
watch a video clip on the call of the first disciples
role-play the call of the first disciples
compose and sing a song on the call of the first four disciples
say how people are called to serve God today
share with peers activities they do in church as service to God
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing a song on the call of the first disciples.
English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners retell the call of the first disciples.

subStrands.name: 3.2 The Temptations of Jesus Christ
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate how Jesus Christ was tempted in the wilderness
identify temptations they face as young people today
desire to overcome temptations in day-to-day life
keyInquiryQuestions: How did Jesus Christ overcome the temptations He faced in the wilderness?
How do you overcome temptations as a young person?
learningExperiences: in pairs, brainstorm on the temptations they face in their daily lives
read Luke 4:1-13 and describe temptations faced by Jesus Christ
discuss how Jesus Christ overcame the temptations He faced in the wilderness
watch a video clip on how Jesus Christ was tempted in the wilderness
in pairs, list the temptations they are likely to face as young people today
team up to discuss how they overcome temptations and share experiences in class
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology skills are applied as learners watch a video clip about Jesus Christ's temptations in the wilderness.
English: reading skills are enhanced as learners read Luke 4:1-13 and retell the story.

subStrands.name: 3.3 Miracles of Jesus Christ — The Roman Officer's Servant
specificLearningOutcomes: narrate the healing of the Roman officer's servant
discuss lessons learnt from the healing of the Roman officer's servant
emulate Jesus Christ's example by praying for the sick
keyInquiryQuestions: How did the Roman officer demonstrate faith in God?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on the importance of praying for the sick
read Matthew 8:5-13 and narrate the miracle
list lessons learnt from the healing of the Roman officer's servant
watch a video clip on the healing of the Roman officer's servant
role play the healing of the Roman officer's servant
share experiences on how they prayed for a sick person
linkedLearningAreas: English: Communication skills are enhanced as learners discuss and read Bible verses.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners role-play the healing of the Roman officer's servant.
Science and Technology skills are applied as learners use digital devices to watch a video clip on the healing of the Roman officer's servant.

subStrands.name: 3.4 Miracle of Healing (Faith in God — the Bleeding Woman)
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the miracle of healing the bleeding woman
identify different ways the church and government help the sick in society
outline lessons learnt from the miracle of healing the bleeding woman
appreciate the healing power of Jesus Christ in their lives
keyInquiryQuestions: How did the bleeding woman portray faith in God?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on what they do when they are sick
in turns, read Luke 8:43-48 and retell the miracle
discuss different ways the church and government are helping the sick and share in class
discuss lessons learnt from the healing of the bleeding woman
compose and sing a song about God's healing power
linkedLearningAreas: Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing songs.
English: communication skills are enhanced as learners read Luke 8:43-48 and retell the miracle.

subStrands.name: 3.5 Raising Lazarus from the Dead
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the miracle of raising Lazarus from the dead
outline lessons learnt from the miracle of raising Lazarus from the dead
appreciate God's power over sickness and death
keyInquiryQuestions: Why did Jesus say that Lazarus was only asleep?
learningExperiences: share how they show empathy to those who have lost family members or friends
discuss how they cope with grief if they lose a close family member or a relative
in pairs, read John 11:32-45 and retell the miracle of raising Lazarus from the dead
outline lessons learnt from raising Lazarus from the dead
compose a poem on 'God's power over sickness and death'
linkedLearningAreas: Social Studies skills are enhanced as learners discuss how to show empathy to those who have lost loved ones.

subStrands.name: 3.6 The Hidden Treasure
specificLearningOutcomes: retell the parable of the hidden treasure
outline lessons learnt from the parable of the hidden treasure
be partakers of the Kingdom of God by committing their lives to Christ
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the Kingdom of God compared to a hidden treasure?
learningExperiences: define the meaning of the word, 'treasure'
state what they treasure most in their lives
brainstorm on the value of the Kingdom of God, 'Why is it so valuable?'
read, in pairs, Matthew 13:44-46 and retell the parable of the hidden treasure
outline lessons learnt from the parable of the hidden treasure
role-play the parable of the hidden treasure
brainstorm on how they can be part of the kingdom of God
share how they respond to the call of salvation in their lives
share with peers the value of the Kingdom of God
compose and sing a song about how valuable the Kingdom of God is
linkedLearningAreas: English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners brainstorm and discuss, in groups, what they value most in their lives.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing a song about the value of the Kingdom of God.

subStrands.name: 3.7 The Rich Man and Lazarus
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the parable of the rich man and Lazarus
discuss lessons learnt from the parable of the rich man and Lazarus
live responsibly as God-fearing Christians
keyInquiryQuestions: How should Christians use their wealth?
learningExperiences: in groups, search from the internet, how Christians use their resources to help people in need
in turns, read Luke 16:19-31 and retell the parable
watch a video clip on the rich man and Lazarus
outline lessons learnt from the parable of the rich man and Lazarus
role-play the parable of the rich man and Lazarus and summarise key points
linkedLearningAreas: Science and Technology skills are applied as learners use digital devices to search for information from the internet.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners role-play the parable of the rich man and Lazarus.

subStrands.name: 4.1 The Apostles' Creed
specificLearningOutcomes: recite the Apostles' Creed to affirm their faith in Christ
outline the teachings outlined in the Apostles' Creed
discuss the importance of the Apostles' Creed to Christians today
list the three persons of the Holy Trinity
recognise the value of the Holy Trinity in their lives
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is the Apostles' Creed important in Christianity?
learningExperiences: recite the Apostle's Creed
write the meaning of Apostles' Creed on charts and display them in the CRE learning corner
summarise the teachings outlined in the Apostle's Creed
state the importance of the Apostles' Creed to Christians today
mention the three persons of the Holy Trinity
compose and sing a song related to Holy Trinity
linkedLearningAreas: English Language: communication skills are enhanced as learners recite the Apostles' Creed.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing a song related to the Holy Trinity.

subStrands.name: 4.2 Standing Firm in Faith — Apostle Paul
specificLearningOutcomes: describe the suffering faced by the Apostles according to 2 Corinthians 6:3-7
identify values/virtues in the life of Apostle Paul
apply values from the life of Apostle Paul in day-to-day life
stand firm in the Christian faith in the face of persecution
keyInquiryQuestions: Why should Christians stand firm in their faith in God?
learningExperiences: brainstorm on how Christians are persecuted in the society today
in turns, read 2 Corinthians 6:3-7 and write down the main points in their exercise books
outline values/virtues in the life of Apostle Paul
practise values learnt from the life of Apostle Paul in daily life

linkedLearningAreas: English: communication skills are enhanced as learners brainstorm on how Christians are persecuted in the society today.
Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners compose and sing relevant songs on standing firm in the Christian faith.

subStrands.name: 4.3 Church Unity
specificLearningOutcomes: explain the meaning of Church unity
explain the biblical teachings on Church unity
describe ways in which Church unity fosters harmonious living

keyInquiryQuestions: Why is Church unity important?
learningExperiences: in pairs, list the different churches in their communities
brainstorm, in small groups, the meaning of Church unity and share with the class
read, in turns, Matthew 16:18, Galatians 3:28 and 1 Corinthians 12:12 and note key points on Church unity

discuss, in pairs, how Christian unity is demonstrated at school and in their communities
identify ways in which different churches work together
watch a video clip on churches working together
compose and sing a song on Church unity

Creative Arts: creative arts skills are applied as learners compose and sing songs related to concepts taught.
Science and Technology skills are enhanced as learners use digital devices to perform various tasks.

subStrands.name: 5.1 Friendship Formation
specificLearningOutcomes: discuss the importance of having good friends
outline biblical teachings on friendship formation
desire to walk with morally upright friends
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to have good friends?
learningExperiences: state qualities to consider in choosing good friends
buzz on how to avoid bad company and negative peer influence
brainstorm on how to choose good friends
discuss the importance of having good friends
read 1 Corinthians 15:33, Proverbs 13:20-21 and Proverbs 16:28-29; discuss lessons learnt and make notes
brainstorm on the topic; 'how to avoid negative peer influence'
linkedLearningAreas: English: speaking skills are enhanced as learners read the Bible Texts and compose poems.
Science and Technology skills are applied as learners use digital devices to make presentation.

subStrands.name: 5.2 Human Sexuality
specificLearningOutcomes: describe biblical teachings on responsible sexual behaviour
outline the causes of irresponsible sexual behaviour among the youth
identify values and life skills required to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour

keyInquiryQuestions: How can you avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour?
learningExperiences: in small groups, list physical and emotional changes that boys and girls experience during adolescence
discuss how to cope with the changes in their bodies during adolescence
in turns, read 1 Corinthians 6:18-20, 2 Timothy 2:22, James 1:14-16 and outline lessons learnt
list some irresponsible sexual behaviour that youths engage in and how to avoid them
in small groups, discuss the causes of irresponsible sexual behaviour
discuss values and life skills required to avoid irresponsible sexual behaviour
compose a poem on, 'My body is the Temple of the Holy Spirit'

subStrands.name: 5.3 Sanctity of Life
specificLearningOutcomes: identify practices that violate the right to life in society today
outline the effects of violating the right to life

keyInquiryQuestions: How can you uphold the sanctity of life?

debate on the topic, 'The effects of violating the right to life'
read Exodus 20:13, Matthew 5:21-24 and write lessons learnt in their exercise books

Social Studies skills are enhanced as learners learn about the right to life.

subStrands.name: 5.4 Alcohol, Drugs and Substance Abuse

keyInquiryQuestions: Why do young people abuse alcohol and drugs?
How can you avoid alcohol, drugs and substance abuse?

brainstorm on the dangers of using and abusing alcohol and drugs
in pairs read Ephesians 5:18, Hosea 4:11 and discuss Christian teachings on the dangers of alcohol, drugs and substance abuse
discuss strategies used by Christians to prevent alcohol, drugs, and substance abuse
in pairs discuss measures taken by government agencies to fight drug trafficking and abuse
discuss values and life skills required to avoid alcohol, drugs and substance abuse
linkedLearningAreas: English: communication skills are enhanced as learners discuss and debate on various concepts.
Social Studies skills are enhanced as learners learn about human rights and responsibilities.
Agriculture skills are enhanced as learners learn the negative effects of abusing alcohol and drugs.
